description: Definitions of hooks/ and scripts/ that look alike and are allowed to coexist because they answer different questions. Read by tests/defs_registry (python3 -m tests.defs_registry), which groups every literal definition by the sameness rule of tests/defs_registry/check.py and fails on a group the register does not split. Each entry: a reason (required) and two or more sides; the definitions of one side answer one question, so two copies on one side are still a duplicate. A definition is identified by its scope-qualified name and the fingerprint of its sorted members (sha256, 16 hex), never by file or line; `at` is where it was when registered. Seeded from the duplicate-definition audit of f199dfb1e: its 61 different-questions families (sides = the distinct member sets of the family) and its ruled-out look-alike pairs (sides = the named definitions).

ceiling.note: tests/defs_registry/test_defs_registry.py fails when this tree has more uncovered groups, or more definitions in them, than this; lower it as merges land, never raise it to admit a new copy. The goal is 0 and 0.

Same function: the long forms, then the short forms by their first two characters.
Three identical tables (git_clean_guard, git-privilege-guard, tool-policy); scripts/capture-hero-run.py:119 GIT_ROUTING_VARS scrubs the environment of a recorded demo run.
The lexer's glob characters, the shell-glob metacharacters of a command-side token, and the characters that make a path after -- wide are three different tests.
VALID_CONFIDENCES is every confidence an edge may carry; the inline set is the confidences that are not yet certain and may be promoted.
Each set is the compound-command kinds one walker treats alike for its own purpose (plain compounds, a stage's output, a cd scope).
doc-sync's excluded patterns, the command-span bookkeeping trees and the overnight guard's state prefixes are three different exemptions of project directories.

Ten tables ask 'is this a here-document' ({<< <<-}), three ask 'does this redirect feed text' (with <<<). f11_options: bash <<<, <<EOF and <<-EOF payloads are refused alike by six hooks.
CLAIM_REGIONS are the README hero regions that hold claims; PROSE_REGIONS the regions whose rows render as prose.

brace/glob/lit asks whether a word part is read as written, glob/lit whether it is a plain literal or glob, brace/glob whether it expands, and Part.inner which parts nest active parts.
Successive steps of one make option walk: the long options spelled with =, then the option words taking a separate value.
The two inline sets are the makefile names make reads; _CODE_FILES are the lower-cased file names whose content a tool runs, gitconfig included.
ALWAYS_ALLOWED decides; INFLIGHT_ALLOWED is 'The whitelist as origin/master (2acc29b) listed it, for the in-flight (D15) wording of a refusal' (the refusal text lists 12 tools while 16 are allowed).
curl's and sort's output options and sort's two forbidden options; the tool policy's own sort -o reading is gone: sort -o is the parser's write target (writer-programs).
Two identical pairs in one file: the actors, and the actors plus a worktree context.
chgrp/chmod/chown, and the same plus touch as 'keeps the content'.

The runtime-guard sets are tokens that start a new command word or are not exec words; RECORDED_REDIRECTION_OPS are the redirections the evidence check accepts in a recorded command.
The two sets are successive tests of removal_policy: the verdicts that authorise a command, and every verdict it knows.

Searcher names for five different tests (the grep guard handles only grep/egrep/fgrep because only grep is shadowed; strict-shape searchers; process selectors). That `ag`/`ack` reads are refused by the harness-switch rule is recorded under reader-programs.
graphify's sensitive-data fragments keep files out of a graph; SECRET_TOKENS and the key-type alternation decide whether a path name is a secret for the bash guard.

File names in the harness home the switch rule protects; the settings layers of the capability binding.

entries.source: lane defs-git (git-all-subcommands, undecided in the audit)
entries.reason: bash_execution_boundary.GIT_SUBCOMMANDS lists the subcommands whose operands the removal policy may call data (it marks them inert); git_command_classifier._GIT_SUBCOMMANDS is every word git takes as a verb, to see a verb after a computed word. The classifier-only names include filter-branch, difftool, mergetool, send-email and instaweb, which run commands they are handed: merged into the removal policy table they would become inert.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family cd-builtins (undecided)
entries.reason: shell_parse.CWD_BUILTINS names the builtins that change the working directory of what follows (cd, pushd, popd); runtime_guard._NAV_OPERAND_HEADS names heads whose trailing words are a directory operand and so data, never a command to launch, and holds chdir, which bash does not have (`chdir /tmp` is command not found and moves nothing), so it cannot join the first.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family package-managers (undecided)
entries.reason: runtime_guard._PM_AT_VERSION_RE names the package managers corepack proxies (corepack yarn|pnpm|npm[@version]; corepack has no bun shim), shell_parse.NODE_PKG_MANAGERS the node package managers the runtime guard reads, bun included.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family shell-set-options (undecided)
entries.reason: bash_safety_rules._HB_INERT_SET lists the -o values a shell invocation (bash -o X -c ...) may carry and stay readable, noexec and posix included because that reader follows noexec and needs no later word read differently; the degraded set reader's value_ok list (_DG_SET_OPTS) accepts on a later `set -o` only the four that change nothing a later word means, so noexec (later commands not run) and posix (parsing changes) are out.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family shell-long-bool-options (undecided)
entries.reason: bash_execution_boundary.SHELL_LONG_BOOL is bash's long options that take no value (for splitting a shell's options); bash_safety_rules._HB_SHELL_LONG the long options the harmless-bash reader can read at all (others make the reading None); _HB_INERT_LONG the subset that leaves the run inert (not --login, which reads profile files, nor --verbose, which echoes the script). Three questions; bash --help decides only the first.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family wrapper-cwd-options (undecided)
entries.reason: runtime_guard._WRAPPER_CWD_OPTS is the union of the cwd options of every wrapper (env -C/--chdir, sudo -D/--chdir, doas -C, systemd-run --working-directory) and _WRAPPER_CWD_SHORT_FUSABLE its short ones that fuse a value; _mutation_targets_for_verb's (-C, --directory) are tar's archive directory, not a wrapper option.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family container-exec-subcommands (undecided)
entries.reason: The removal analyzer's _h_kubectl reads kubectl's subcommands that run a command in a pod (exec, run, debug); _docker_sub reads docker's that run one in a container (exec, run, create: docker create takes the command it later starts). Two programs, two subcommand sets.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family container-launchers (undecided)
entries.reason: git_command_classifier._EXEC_LAUNCHERS names the container launchers whose exec/run arguments may run git (docker, podman, kubectl); bash_safety_rules._DG_READ_HANDLERS names the commands the degraded reader has its own subcommand handler for (git, docker, kubectl, find, hash, ssh). A launcher set and a dispatch table.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, audit f199dfb1e family pm-builtin-subcommands (undecided)
entries.reason: constants.DEP_BUILTINS is the dependency-management subcommands common to npm, yarn, pnpm and bun (install, add, remove ...), the guard's P9 dependency-op rule; _core._PM_SUBCMDS is npm's full builtin list with its typo aliases (install-test, isntall, ...), read to find npm's subcommand word past its options, and holds words (build, test, start) that yarn and pnpm run as package scripts; DEP_SHORTHAND_NPM is npm's four lifecycle shorthands (start, stop, restart, test) that RUN a script. Three questions.
tar's -f/--file names the archive it reads or writes; grep's -f/--file names a file of patterns: two programs' options spelled alike.

The disk guard's _DG_FIND_WORDS is the whole find grammar it admits; the userintent rule's two sets are the words it skips before reading -exec and those of them that take a value; the runtime guard's _FIND_PREPATH_ARG_OPTS the depth options (find's and fd's) that may come before the start paths. Each is a different reading of find.

_PY_READER_MODULES are modules that, run with python -m, only read the files named; _PY_SAFE_MODULES are modules whose import in -c code loads no other code and runs nothing. A module can be either without the other (json.tool vs math).

entries.source: defs-shell lane, check group on integration a839e0c9a
entries.reason: shell_parse.PRINTERS (echo, printf: programs that print their arguments and run nothing) is the one definition the Python hooks read; scripts/canary-verify.sh asks the same of a script's lines with grep -E in bash and cannot import a Python table, so its pattern is the shell-side copy.

entries.source: defs-shell lane, check group on integration a839e0c9a
entries.reason: shell_parse.WriteTarget.placed leaves a path that starts with /, ~, $ or a backquote as written when it reports where a write lands (a computed path cannot be joined to a cd directory); the config guard's _parsed_kind decides which candidate paths to test against the protected folders and joins every text but an absolute, home or $-led one to each cd directory, a backquote-led one included, so it tests more candidates and refuses at least as often. Different questions; merging would drop the guard's extra candidates.
